title: Adding a 5% stop to a SPY trend rule cost $9,000 and made the drawdown worse
author: person-person12
selftext:
Every risk lesson in trading says never sit in a position without a stop under it, so I put one on the plainest trend rule there is and measured what it actually did to the account.

The rule: buy SPY at the close when it closes above its 200 day average, sell when it closes back below. Daily candles, January 2001 to March 2026, $10k to start, commission and slippage charged on both sides of every fill. I ran it twice in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading), once bare and once with a hard stop 5% under the entry, everything else identical.

**Bare:** 83 trades, 34.9% of them won, profit factor 2.80, finished at **$40,006**, worst drawdown 22.1%.

**With the 5% stop:** 87 trades, 32.2% won, profit factor 2.36, finished at **$30,990**, worst drawdown 26.3%.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

The stop fired **5 times in 25 years** and those five trades lost $2,459 between them. Four of the five bought back in within three days at a higher price than the stop had just sold at, and the worst of them sold December 20th 2004 at 107.29 and was back in the next day at 119.63. The rest of the $9,016 gap is compounding, since every stopped out position sizes the one behind it off a smaller account.

March 2020 is the part I didnt expect going in. The stop never got touched. Price came through the 200 day average before it fell 5% from the entry, so the trend exit closed the position in both runs and the protective level was never reached at all.

So the drawdown went the wrong way, **26.3% with the stop against 22.1% without it**, on the same rule over the same 25 years.

comments.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
comments.body:
"buy SPY at the close when it closes above its 200 day average, sell when it closes back below. "

So you are buying when it is high and selling when it is low?

Also, the old rule that I always heard is that if the asset you buy falls to under 7% down then you need to work on your entries. So I suspect those 5% cuts were too shallow and cut out reversals that would have paid off later. For holding stocks the rule is time in market is more important that timing the market.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Yea thats trend following in one sentence, you pay for a late entry and a late exit and hope the trends run long enough to cover both. And **your read on the 5% was exactly what happened,** the stop kept cutting dips that came back, which is why the drawdown got worse instead of better.

replies.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
replies.body: Yeah, everyone's first move is to set tight stops. But for real pay off, most of the time you have to hang more out there. MM with hunt retail stops, before blowing up. You stop out at -10% and 2 minutes later it would have been +100%.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Yea wider would have helped this one. The 5% stop wasnt protecting anything, it was **selling the position at the bottom of a drop that recovered anyway**, and then the trend rule bought it back higher a few weeks later. The drawdown came out worse with the stop on than with it off.

replies.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
